entry.title: How Companies Are Approaching MCP: Reflections From Amsterdam
entry.content:
AGNTCon + MCPCon Europe took place in Amsterdam on 17–18 September 2026 as part of the Agentic AI Foundation’s community events. It brought together protocol maintainers, open-source contributors and enterprise engineering teams to discuss MCP and the infrastructure needed to put agents into practice. Across the keynotes and technical sessions, a recurring question was how open standards can help agents work with tools and services across different platforms.

As an architect in SAP’s Cross Product Alignment team, I work on MCP architecture and guidance. My work also includes contributing to the MCP Server Card initiative and discussions on discovery metadata as part of SAP’s contributions to the MCP community within the Agentic AI Foundation. The conference offered a chance to look beyond our own work at SAP and hear how companies are approaching integration, discovery and agent execution.

Putting MCP into practice involves more than connecting an agent to a tool. Teams are deciding how capabilities are discovered, what information enters the model’s context and how access is managed. These choices become increasingly important as MCP use grows from individual experiments into shared services.

 

A Protocol That Is Easier To Operate At Scale

 

The MCP protocol updates highlighted in the keynote addresses practical challenges in running MCP across distributed systems. The July 2026 revision of the protocol introduces a stateless core, replacing the initialization handshake and protocol-level sessions with protocol version and capability information carried on each request. This reduces the need to tie a client’s requests to a particular server instance. Applications can still retain business state through explicit handles.

Multi-round-trip requests address another operational concern: waiting for additional input. A server can return a request for information, allowing the client to gather it and resubmit the request with that information without keeping a stream open throughout the wait.

The revision also introduces cache hints for resource and capability responses, alongside standardized HTTP headers that make MCP operations more visible to infrastructure components.

Together, these changes support deployment through existing service infrastructure. Application state and safe retry handling remain implementation responsibilities, even when the protocol itself is stateless.

 

From Individual Integrations To Shared Infrastructure

 

The sessions on enterprise adoption explored how shared infrastructure can support MCP use across teams. The approaches presented combined catalogs, gateways and publishing processes to give teams a common way to discover, access and publish integrations while allowing developers to choose among supported agent clients.

An important part of this approach is the division of responsibility. Teams retain ownership of their integrations, while shared infrastructure provides connectivity, validation and publication checks. Making a server available also creates responsibilities for maintaining it, reviewing changes and helping others find it.

As organizations expose more capabilities, these responsibilities become harder to handle through individual configurations. Discovery metadata, ownership and access controls need to be considered as part of the integration from the beginning.

 

Progressive Tool Discovery And The Role Of The Harness

 

The discussions on context management highlighted an important distinction: loading every tool definition into model context upfront is a client implementation choice, rather than a requirement of MCP.

The harness coordinates the model, context and tool execution. It determines which tool information reaches the model and how intermediate results are handled. Progressive tool discovery allows a client to reveal capabilities gradually, retrieving detailed definitions when they become relevant to a task.

This can reduce the information loaded upfront, but discovery also has a cost. Additional searches or repeated attempts can offset the savings. The useful question is whether selective loading helps the agent complete its task reliably and efficiently.

Context management needs to be evaluated as part of the complete workflow. A smaller initial set of tool definitions can be useful, but the agent still needs to find the appropriate tools and use them correctly.

Progressive tool discovery compared with loading all tool definitions upfront. AI-generated conceptual illustration, reviewed by the author. It does not represent benchmark results.

 

 

How Tools Are Executed Matters Too

 

The conference discussions on tool execution also explored how command-line interfaces can work together with MCP. A related article on progressive discovery and shell composition illustrates how a CLI can use the harness’s existing MCP connections. This allows the agent to inspect available tools and filter their results through shell commands before returning the relevant information to the model.

This shows why MCP and CLI do not always need to be treated as competing choices. MCP can provide the connection to a capability, while a CLI or code execution environment provides a way to compose calls and process results.

An illustrative example of this pattern would be an agent summarising overdue invoices. Using a CLI connected to the harness’s MCP tools, it could retrieve invoice records and pass them to code that filters overdue items and calculates totals by customer and currency. In this setup, the execution environment could process the records and return only the resulting summary data to the model. MCP provides access to the tool, while the execution environment processes the data before the model writes the summary.

Discovery and execution therefore need to be considered together. How much information enters the model’s context? Which intermediate steps can be handled programmatically? Where are permissions enforced? Those choices help explain an integration’s behaviour beyond the interface used to invoke it.

 

Skills Bring Guidance Closer To Capabilities

 

The session on Skills over MCP was particularly interesting to me because it addresses what happens after a capability becomes available. A tool contract describes an operation and its inputs. A skill can provide workflow instructions, examples and supporting references that help an agent use several operations together.

The Skills over MCP extension allows servers to distribute these instructions and supporting files through MCP. Clients can discover skills and retrieve their contents when needed. The host remains responsible for how a skill is selected, loaded and presented to the model. Retrieving a file does not automatically activate it.

This creates an architectural question: which guidance should belong to the capability provider, and which decisions should remain with the harness?

The provider understands the service and its intended workflows. The harness manages the current task, available context and execution environment. Keeping that division explicit could help providers deliver useful guidance without assuming that every client behaves identically.

A related proposal discussed at the conference was applying semantic versioning to skills. Changes to instructions can change agent behavior, so those instructions also deserve lifecycle management.

 

Tool Discovery Starts Before The Connection

 

Progressive disclosure helps an agent select tools from available providers. In a larger landscape, there is an earlier question: how does the agent find the relevant provider in the first place?

@sebastian_wennemersand I explored this question in our session, “From API Catalogs to Agent Catalogs.” Through a spacecraft story and live demo, we showcased how Open Resource Discovery and MCP Server Cards can work together to support discovery before a client connects to a server.

ORD provides a way to publish and aggregate resource metadata, helping consumers find relevant MCP servers across a larger landscape. MCP Server Cards complement this by describing individual servers and how to connect to them. Together, they help address the discovery challenge at two levels: finding a relevant provider and understanding how to access it.

Since the conference, SEP-2127 on MCP Server Cards has reached Final status. Our demo also explored including tool metadata in the Server cards to help consumers assess relevance before connecting. This goes beyond the finalized design, with tool metadata being explored as future work in the Server Card community.

The audience was curious about how these pieces fit together and could be applied in practice. Those conversations reinforced the importance of making capabilities discoverable, alongside making them available.

 

What This Means For Developers And Architects

 

For teams building with MCP, the conference discussions suggest evaluating the full path from a user’s request to a completed task.

Can the agent find the appropriate provider? Does it receive the tool definitions and guidance it needs at the right time? Can the harness coordinate execution reliably, with clear permissions and ownership?

For organizations with mature APIs and integration infrastructure, there is another question: where does MCP improve interoperability across agent clients or make business capabilities easier to use? That benefit needs to justify the additional layer that teams will maintain.

These are practical questions to bring into architecture reviews and evaluations. Comparing complete workflows can help teams identify which choices actually improve the outcome.

Where is your team encountering the most difficulty: exposing capabilities, helping agents discover them, or making their use reliable within a workflow?

※免責事項

本稿は JSUG テクニカル部会のオピニオンリーダーとしての個人の見解であり、JSUG の公式な見解ではありません。セッションの集計と文章の一部には生成AIを使っています。内容の正確性は保証できませんので、情報の活用はご自身の判断でお願いします。

この記事のポイント

  • SAP TechEd Berlin 2026（308件）と ASUG Tech Connect 2026（176件）の公開セッションカタログを、参加前に全件数えてみました。
  • どちらも主役は AI エージェントです（セッションの4〜5割）。TechEd では、AI を「作る」トラックより「設計・運用・保護する」トラックのほうが大きく、全社の AI ガバナンスも独立したトラックになっています。
  • 5月の Sapphire で発表された Joule Work、SAP AI Agent Hub、Joule Studio などは、TechEd ではハンズオンや顧客の話として出てきます。一方で、Anthropic や NVIDIA の名前はカタログに出てきません。
  • ASUG は、移行・費用・ガバナンス・規制の比率が TechEd の2〜3倍です。TechEd は「移行を AI で速くする」、ASUG は「AI のために足元を整える」という向きで、SAP の Christian Klein 氏と ASUG の Geoff Scott 氏の最近の発言もそれぞれ同じ方向を指しています。
  • 現地で見てきたことは、12月8日の JSUG Conference と、1月に予定しているテクニカル部会でお届けします。

はじめに

10月27日から29日まで、ベルリンで SAP TechEd が開かれます。その1週間後、11月2日から4日には米国フォートワースで ASUG Tech Connect があります。JSUG テクニカル部会からは、今年も両方にメンバーが参加します。私はベルリンに行きます。

昨年は ASUG Tech Connect に参加したあとでレポートを書きました。今年は、行く前に書いてみることにしました。

きっかけは出発前の下調べです。どの回に出るかを決めようと公開のセッションカタログを眺めていたのですが、数が多くて目では追いきれません。そこで 、TechEd と ASUG Tech Connect のカタログを全件取得し、形式・トラック・キーワードで数えてみました。すると、一覧を眺めているだけでは気づかなかった傾向がいくつか見えてきました。

これから参加する方、オンラインで見る予定の方、今年は見送る方にも、全体をつかむ材料になればと思ってまとめておきます。数字はすべて10月6日時点の公開カタログによるものです。

1. おさらい：SAP のイベントの位置づけ

ご存じの方も多いと思いますが、簡単におさらいしておきます。SAP が自ら主催する大きなイベントは、今は次の3つです。

  • SAP Sapphire（5月）：経営と事業の発表。オーランド会場は ASUG の年次大会と合同です

TechEd には地域版（TechEd on Tour）があり、北米では ASUG Tech Connect がその役割を担っています。日本向けには SAP ジャパンによるオンラインの SAP TechEd Japan があり、JSUG ではメンバーが現地に行って、JSUG Conference等 で報告しています。

2. 今年の流れ：5月に構想、10月に提供開始、そして技術の中身へ

今年の SAP は、5月の Sapphire で「自律型企業（Autonomous Enterprise）」と SAP Business AI Platform を打ち出しました。50以上のアシスタントと200以上のエージェントという構想が示されています。

10月上旬の SAP Connect では、その仕組みの一般提供が始まることが発表されました。ただし、個別のアシスタントの多くは2026年末から2027年初めにかけての提供予定です。

その流れで迎えるのが今回の TechEd です。経営向けに語られた構想が、技術者向けにはどういう中身として語られるのか。今年はそこを見る回だと思っています。

3. Sapphire の発表は、TechEd でどう形になっているか

5月の Sapphire で発表されたものが TechEd でどう扱われているかを、カタログで追ってみました。発表の段階だったものが、ハンズオンや顧客の話として出てきています。

  • Joule Work：Sapphire で紹介された、Joule を中心にした新しい作業画面です。TechEd では25件のセッションに登場し、デスクトップ・モバイル・Web で動かすハンズオン（JW163・JW164・JW261）があります。JW206 では、製造・小売・企業 IT で本番運用している顧客の話が紹介されるようです。
  • SAP AI Agent Hub：Sapphire で「7〜9月に提供」とされたエージェントの台帳です。TechEd では、エージェントの発見から廃止までを試すハンズオン（BT161）と、SAP 自身が社内でどう使っているかの回（BT116）が並びます。
  • Joule Studio：51件と、いちばん多く登場します。自分でエージェントを作るハンズオンが複数あるほか、SAP Build から Joule Studio への移行の進め方（AD106）や、移行を準備している製造業 Knapp の話（ST126）もあります。
  • Joule のアシスタント：調達（AS264 Sourcing Assistant）や決算（AS260 Financial Closing Assistant）のアシスタントを実際に触れるハンズオンがあります。
  • SAP Business Data Cloud：データをコピーせずに共有するハンズオン（DA162）や、Henkel で SAP と Adobe のエージェントが連携する事例（DA206）があります。

一方で、Sapphire で大きく取り上げられた外部のパートナー、Anthropic（Claude）と NVIDIA の名前は、TechEd のカタログには一度も出てきません。Databricks も4件だけです。カタログに書かれていないだけで中身として扱われないとは限りませんが、TechEd では「SAP の製品として何ができるか」に話が集中しているように見えます。

4. TechEd Berlin 2026 のカタログを数えてみた

TechEd Berlin のセッションは308件あります。

まず感じたのは、主役がはっきりしていることです。タイトルか概要に AI エージェントが出てくるセッションは144件、全体の47%でした。製品名で多いのも SAP Business AI Platform、Joule、Joule Studio です。

意外だったのはトラックの構成です。9本あるトラックのうち最大は「Architect, operate, and secure AI at scale（AI の設計・運用・保護）」で57件。エージェントやアプリを「作る」トラック（49件）より多いのです。さらに「Drive AI governance for enterprise-wide impact（全社の AI ガバナンス）」が独立したトラックとして27件あります。中身を見ると、エージェントの台帳（SAP AI Agent Hub）、監視（SAP Cloud ALM）、SAP 自身の社内での運用事例などが並んでいます。AI を作る話から、作ったものをどう管理するかの話へ、重心が少しずつ移ってきているように見えます。

6. Clean Core と S/4HANA 移行はどう扱われているか

AI エージェント一色に見えるカタログですが、Clean Core や S/4HANA（SAP Cloud ERP）への移行の話がなくなったわけではありません。TechEd には「Accelerate and de-risk transformation（移行・変革）」というトラックがあり、35件あります。

TechEd で目につくのは、移行の作業そのものに AI を使う回です。たとえば次のような回があります。

  • TM105「Agent-led custom code migration: From planning to mass adaptation」（アドオンの移行をエージェントで進める）
  • TM263「AI-accelerated RISE with SAP migration with the system transition workbench」（ハンズオン）
  • TM108「The journey with clean core continues for SAP Cloud ERP Private」
  • XP110「Beyond migration: Turning Neo sunset into strategic platform transformation」（Neo 環境の終了への対応）

ASUG のほうは顧客事例が中心で、どちらかというと「AI を本格的に使うには、まず Clean Core とデータを整える」という順番で語られています。HP・Jabil・Bristol Myers Squibb が登壇する「AI at Scale Starts with a Clean Core」、Florida Crystals が4週間で Clean Core の評価をした事例、Costco の移行の自動化、Hershey の RISE と Business Data Cloud の事例などです。上の表でも、移行の比率は TechEd の7%に対して ASUG は20%、クリーンコアは3%に対して9%でした。

TechEd は「移行を AI で速くする」、ASUG は「AI のために足元を整える」。同じ Clean Core と AI の組み合わせを、提供側と利用側が逆の向きから語っているように見えます。昨年の記事でも Clean Core は両イベントに共通するテーマでしたが、今年は AI と組になって語られるようになっています。

7. 両トップの最近の発言も、同じ方向を指している

カタログの傾向は、SAP と ASUG のトップの最近の発言とも重なります。

SAP の Christian Klein 氏は、5月の Sapphire の基調講演で、公開データで学習した汎用の LLM だけでは基幹業務には足りないと述べています。消費者向けの AI なら8割の正確さでも許されるが企業ではそうはいかない、という趣旨で、「Eighty percent is just not good enough」と表現しました。データのモデルが壊れていれば、どんなエージェントでも補えない、とも話しています。10月の SAP Connect の記者会見では、文脈（コンテキスト）とガバナンスはセットだと強調し、3年がかりの移行の時代は終わったとも語ったと報じられています。TechEd で AI の運用と保護のトラックが最大になり、Knowledge Graph の回や移行を AI で進める回が並んでいるのは、この方針がそのまま技術の中身になったものと読めます。

一方、昨年の記事でも紹介した ASUG の Geoff Scott 氏は、10月に公開された ASUG の S/4HANA 調査の紹介で、会員の関心は「S/4HANA に移ること」から「S/4HANA で価値を出すこと」に移り、定着やガバナンス、稼働後の取り組みに向いていると話しています。8月のインタビューでは、エージェントは整ったデータに頼るので、顧客や品目をどう定義するかといったマスターデータのガバナンスを、判断を任せる前に決めておく必要があると指摘しました。今は実験することが何より大事だ、とも述べています。ASUG のカタログで移行・費用・ガバナンスの比率が高く、「AI のためにまず足元を整える」顧客事例が並ぶのと、ちょうど同じ向きです。

面白いのは、二人とも「データと文脈とガバナンスが先」という点では一致していることです。違うのはその先で、SAP は「だから SAP の基盤とクラウドで」、ASUG は「だから、まず自分たちのデータを整えよう」と続きます。TechEd と ASUG の違いは、この立ち位置の違いがそのまま出たものなのかもしれません。

8. 日本の会社は登場するか

少し気になって、登壇者の所属も調べてみました。TechEd Berlin では、登壇者（延べ675人）の所属に日本企業は見当たりませんでした。

ASUG Tech Connect では、日本にゆかりのある会社の米国拠点の事例が2つあります。DIC グループの Sun Chemical による API のモダナイゼーションと SAP BTP の事例と、2019年にパナソニックから独立した i-PRO Americas による受注処理の自動化の事例です。i-PRO の回の紹介文には、日本のチームも関心を持っていると書かれています。

ちなみに5月の Sapphire（オーランド）には、ダイキン、富士通、武田薬品などの事例があり、SuccessFactors の基調講演にはトヨタの方も登壇していました。経営と事業の場である Sapphire には日本企業の名前が出てくるのに、技術の場ではまだ少ない。日本のユーザーが技術の話をする側に回れるとよいな、と思います。

ここからは個人の関心です。私は AI を作る話よりも、作ったものを企業としてどう管理するかに関心があります。今年はちょうど、そこが TechEd の大きな柱になっているので楽しみにしています。具体的には、次のようなことを確かめてきたいと思っています。

  • エージェントの台帳と統制は、SAP 以外のエージェントまでどこまで見られるのか

Disclaimer:

This article reflects my personal views as an Opinion Leader of the JSUG Technical SIG and does not represent the official views of JSUG. Key points

  • Before attending, I counted every session in the public catalogs of SAP TechEd Berlin 2026 (308 sessions) and ASUG Tech Connect 2026 (176 sessions).
  • AI agents are the main theme of both events (40–50% of sessions). At TechEd, the track on architecting, operating, and securing AI is larger than the track on building agents and apps, and enterprise-wide AI governance has its own track.

  • What we learn on site will be shared at the JSUG Conference on December 8 and at the JSUG Technical SIG meeting planned for January.

Introduction

SAP TechEd takes place in Berlin from October 27 to 29. A week later, from November 2 to 4, ASUG Tech Connect is held in Fort Worth, Texas. As in previous years, members of the JSUG (Japan SAP Users' Group) Technical SIG will attend both events. I will be going to Berlin.

Last year, I wrote a report after attending ASUG Tech Connect. This year, I decided to write something before I go.

It started as preparation for the trip. I was looking through the public session catalogs to decide which sessions to attend, but there were simply too many to follow by eye. I collected every session from the TechEd and ASUG Tech Connect catalogs and counted them by format, track, and keyword. A few trends emerged that I would not have noticed just by scrolling through the lists.

I hope this gives a useful overview to those attending, those watching online, and those skipping this year. All figures are based on the public catalogs as of October 6.

1. A quick recap: SAP's major events

Many readers will already know this, but here is a brief recap. SAP currently hosts three major events of its own:

  • SAP Sapphire (May): Strategy and business announcements. The Orlando event is held jointly with the ASUG Annual Conference.
  • SAP Connect (October): For line-of-business users. It brought together the separate events for HR, procurement, finance, and other areas into one in 2025.
  • SAP TechEd (October): For IT professionals and technologists.

TechEd also has regional editions (TechEd on Tour), and in North America ASUG Tech Connect plays that role. In Japan, SAP Japan holds the online SAP TechEd Japan, and JSUG sends members to the events and reports back at the JSUG Conference or etc.

2. This year's flow: vision in May, availability in October, then the technical details

At Sapphire in May, SAP introduced the "Autonomous Enterprise" and the SAP Business AI Platform, with a vision of more than 50 assistants and more than 200 agents.

At SAP Connect in early October, SAP announced that general availability of these capabilities is starting. Many of the individual assistants, however, are planned for late 2026 to early 2027.

TechEd comes next in this flow. I see this year's TechEd as the place to find out what the vision presented to executives looks like in technical terms.

3. How Sapphire announcements are taking shape at TechEd

I used the catalog to trace how the Sapphire announcements appear at TechEd. Things that were announcements in May now show up as hands-on workshops and customer stories.

  • Joule Work: The new Joule-centered workspace introduced at Sapphire. It appears in 25 TechEd sessions, including hands-on workshops on the desktop, mobile, and web experiences (JW163, JW164, JW261). JW206 is described as featuring customers who run it in production in manufacturing, retail, and enterprise IT.
  • SAP AI Agent Hub: The agent inventory that Sapphire said would be available in Q3. TechEd offers a hands-on workshop covering agents from discovery to decommissioning (BT161) and a session on how SAP uses it internally (BT116).
  • Joule Studio: The most frequent, appearing in 51 sessions. There are several hands-on workshops for building your own agents, a session on the transition path from SAP Build to Joule Studio (AD106), and a story from the manufacturer Knapp, which is preparing for that transition (ST126).
  • Joule assistants: Hands-on workshops let you try assistants for sourcing (AS264, Sourcing Assistant) and financial closing (AS260, Financial Closing Assistant).
  • SAP Business Data Cloud: A hands-on workshop on sharing data products without copies (DA162) and a Henkel case in which SAP and Adobe agents work together (DA206).

On the other hand, Anthropic (Claude) and NVIDIA, the external partners highlighted at Sapphire, are not mentioned anywhere in the TechEd catalog, and Databricks appears only four times. Not being in the catalog does not mean they will not be covered, but TechEd seems to focus on what SAP's own products can do.

4. Counting the SAP TechEd Berlin 2026 catalog

TechEd Berlin has 308 sessions.

The first thing I noticed is how clear the main theme is. AI agents appear in the title or abstract of 144 sessions, or 47% of the total. The most frequent products are SAP Business AI Platform, Joule, and Joule Studio.

What surprised me was the track structure. Of the nine tracks, the largest is "Architect, operate, and secure AI at scale" with 57 sessions, more than the track for building agents, workflows, and applications (49). Looking inside, you find the agent inventory (SAP AI Agent Hub), monitoring (SAP Cloud ALM), and SAP's own internal operations. The center of gravity seems to be shifting gradually from building AI to managing what has been built.

6. Clean core and S/4HANA migration

The catalogs may look as if they are all about AI agents, but clean core and migration to S/4HANA (SAP Cloud ERP) have not gone away. TechEd has a track called "Accelerate and de-risk transformation" with 35 sessions.

What stands out at TechEd are sessions that use AI for the migration work itself. For example:

7. Recent remarks by both leaders point the same way

The catalog trends also match recent remarks by the leaders of SAP and ASUG.

In his Sapphire keynote in May, SAP's Christian Klein said that general-purpose LLMs trained on public data are not enough for mission-critical business. Consumer AI may get away with 80% accuracy, but businesses cannot, as he put it: "Eighty percent is just not good enough." He also said that no agent can make up for a broken data model. At the SAP Connect press Q&A in October, he reportedly stressed that context and governance go together and declared the end of three-year migrations. The fact that the AI operations and security track is the largest at TechEd, alongside sessions on the Knowledge Graph and AI-driven migration, can be read as this direction turning into technical content.

Meanwhile, ASUG's Geoff Scott, whom I also quoted in last year's article, said in October, when ASUG's S/4HANA research was published, that members' attention has shifted from getting to S/4HANA to getting value from it, with a focus on adoption, governance, and post-go-live work. In an interview in August, he pointed out that agents depend on clean, consistent data, so companies need to decide how to govern master data, such as how to define a customer or a product, before they hand decisions over to agents. He also said that experimenting is the most important thing right now. This fits well with the higher share of migration, cost, and governance in the ASUG catalog and its customer stories about getting the foundation ready for AI.

What I find interesting is that both agree that data, context, and governance come first. The difference is what follows. SAP continues with "so use SAP's platform and the cloud," while ASUG continues with "so let's get our own data in order first." The difference between TechEd and ASUG may simply reflect this difference in standpoint.

8. Do Japanese companies appear?

Out of curiosity, I also checked the speakers' companies. At TechEd Berlin, I found no Japanese companies among the speakers (675 speaker slots in total).

At ASUG Tech Connect, there are two sessions from US operations of companies with Japanese roots: Sun Chemical, part of the DIC Group, on API modernization and SAP BTP, and i-PRO Americas, which became independent from Panasonic in 2019, on automating order processing. The i-PRO session description mentions that its team in Japan is also interested.

By contrast, Sapphire Orlando in May included cases from Daikin, Fujitsu, and Takeda, and a speaker from Toyota appeared in the SuccessFactors keynote. Japanese companies show up at Sapphire, the business-focused event, but are still rare at the technical events. I hope more Japanese users will take the stage to talk about technology.

9. What I want to see on site

This part is my personal interest. I am more interested in how companies manage AI than in how they build it. This year, that happens to be one of TechEd's main pillars, so I am looking forward to it. Specifically, I want to find out:

  • How far the agent inventory and governance can see, including non-SAP agents
  • How usage-based pricing for AI (AI Units) looks to users and how it can be managed
  • How ready, in practice, it is to hand migration and custom code rework over to agents

For hands-on workshops, I plan to join the AI-enabled tabletop exercise for cyber resilience (XP160) and the SAP Company Memory preview (BT162).

Closing

The numbers in the catalog only show what is planned. What is actually said on stage and what attendees react to can only be seen on site.

Sharing what we bring back

We plan to share what we see and hear at the following two events:

  • JSUG Conference 2026, Tuesday, December 8: In the Technical SIG session "B-2: Sharing the Latest SAP Technology Updates from SAP TechEd and ASUG Tech Connect 2026" (11:15–12:00, in Japanese), members who attended TechEd and ASUG Tech Connect will share the latest information from the events.
    Registration: https://www.jsug.org/conference2026
  • JSUG Technical SIG meeting in January: Attending members will cover their topics in more detail. I will add the date and registration information to this article once they are announced, along with a link to the materials after the meeting.

Both events are open to JSUG members. Please see the JSUG website for details.

What I wrote here is only my reading before the event. I want to share honestly at both events what turned out as expected and what did not. I hope you can join us.

TechEd keynotes and some sessions will also be streamed online on the same dates (SAP TechEd Virtual), so please take a look even if you are not going this year. If you will be in Berlin, I would be happy if you said hello.

entry.title: From SAP TechEd Berlin to Your Next Blog Post
entry.content:
Hello SAP Community!

I’m Fatemeh Zarei, and I’ve been working with the SAP Community team for over a year now, creating content and helping share stories from across the community.

During this time, I’ve had the opportunity to attend D-COM and SAP Inside Track Hamburg. Attending SAP Inside Track Hamburg gave me the opportunity to enjoy interesting sessions and connect with fellow community members. I’ve always loved events for exactly this reason: the chance to exchange ideas and get to know the people behind the technology. That experience helped me better understand SAP technology and connect with the great SAP community in Hamburg.

That’s also why I enjoy hearing people’s stories after an event. We can attend the same event and come away with completely different experiences. A session you almost skipped might become your biggest takeaway, or a quick conversation might introduce you to someone you’ll stay connected with.

So, why not share your upcoming SAP TechEd Berlin experience with the SAP Community?

You don’t need to be an experienced blogger, and you don’t need to write about everything that happened. A few highlights, useful lessons, or memorable community moments are a great place to start.

Let’s go!

Your SAP TechEd Story: 10 Questions to Get You Started

Use some of the questions below as a starting point for your blog post draft. Choose the ones that are meaningful to you, skip the others, and add anything else you’d like to share.

Who are you, and what brought you to SAP TechEd?

Introduce yourself briefly. Tell readers about your role, your interests, and whether this was your first SAP TechEd.

What were you most looking forward to, and how did the experience compare?

Perhaps you wanted to explore a particular technology, get hands-on experience, or meet fellow community members. Tell us how it went and what surprised you.

Which session stood out to you, and why?

Share what made it worth attending and your main takeaway. Include a link to the session or related resources so readers can explore further.

What technology or idea are you excited to explore further?

Whether it’s SAP Business AI, Joule, application development, integration, or something completely different, tell us what caught your attention and why.

What did you learn that you could apply in your work?

Describe a practical tip, a new approach, or an idea you’d like to try with your colleagues, customers, or projects.

Did a session or conversation change your perspective?

Tell us what you thought before and what made you see things differently. It could be a technical insight or something you learned from another person’s experience.

Who did you connect with, and what made that interaction memorable?

Maybe you met someone you previously knew only online, reconnected with a community friend, or had an unexpected conversation. Share what made that connection special and tag the people you met so they can join the conversation. If you took a picture together, consider including it, with their permission of course 🙂

What was your favorite SAP TechEd moment?

Choose one moment that captures the event for you. If you have a picture, include it and tell us the story behind it: what was happening, who you were with, and why it mattered.

What advice would you give a first-time attendee?

Share a practical tip you wish you’d known beforehand—whether it’s about choosing sessions, preparing for the event, or making time for community activities.

What comes next?

Tell us what you plan to do with what you learned. You might try a new technology, share your takeaways with colleagues, stay in touch with someone you met, or create your next SAP Community contribution.

Now It’s Your Turn! ✨

Your blog post doesn’t have to follow this exact order or answer all ten questions. Choose the ones that help you tell your story and add pictures and useful links along the way.

Before publishing, complete the Tour the SAP Community tutorial if you haven’t already, it’s required for blogging and will help you get familiar with the platform before sharing your story.

Ready to share? Create your blog post in Community Corner and add the SAP TechEd and SAP Community tags so others can find your story.

Finish by inviting readers to join the conversation. You could ask: “What was your biggest SAP TechEd takeaway?”

Most of all, write in your own voice. Your experience and perspective are what make your contribution worth reading.

I’m looking forward to reading your SAP TechEd stories and discovering the sessions, people, and moments that made the event special for you!

Have fun blogging!

entry.title: On my way to my third SAP TechEd
entry.content:
Hello Community,

I’m packing my suitcase because tomorrow I’m leaving for my third SAP TechEd. 🙂

Last year, when I went to Berlin, I had just suffered a significant family loss and wasn’t able to enjoy it the way I would have liked. This year I’m going with a different spirit: I’ve spent months studying and working on new topics, and I’m bringing along a completely different kind of luggage, both technical and emotional.

I can’t wait to share what I’ve learned with anyone who’s interested. Here’s what I’ve been working on this year.

Joule: from low-code to pro-code

I started with low-code in Joule Studio, building skills and agents connected directly to SAP SuccessFactors OData APIs. It was a great starting point, but with more complex scenarios, which require several sequential calls and precise logic, I began to hit its limits. For example, I had to fight with Joule’s routing, which preferred to answer from Document Grounding instead of using my skill.

So I switched to pro-code: I developed an agent integrated with SAP AI Core and exposed it to Joule through the A2A protocol. In the same spirit, I also built an MCP server with CAP to let Joule talk to on-premise document sources through the Cloud Connector.

Along the way I ran into all the classic issues that come with new products: destination and authentication configurations, features that suddenly become opt-in and disappear from your tenant, undocumented behaviors, and small details that cost you hours. Now I can share them so you don’t have to lose those hours yourself.

SAP Document Grounding

I worked on integrating Document Grounding into an HR scenario related to SAP SuccessFactors, learning first-hand the configuration limits of the pipelines and how to work around them.

Identity and authorizations

For anyone who needs it: I tackled connecting an ECC system with SAP Cloud Identity Services (IAS/IPS) to orchestrate roles and groups, and mapping groups to Role Collections in SAP BTP.

Certifications

This year I also earned several SAP certifications, from ABAP Cloud and BTP to the new AI ones. Preparing for them helped me put structure around everything I had been doing in the field.

If you’d like to exchange ideas, you’ll find me around the Community Clubhouse. Come and say hi in person, and feel free to ask me for advice based on my experience.

And while you’re at it, why not complete the missions launched by @MariettaLopez  in Catch and Know an SAP Champion or an SAP Mentor Missions? Grab a selfie with me for #CatchAChampion, and if you’re up for it, a real conversation for #KnowAChampion. I’d be happy to be your mission!

See you there!

entry.title: SAP HANA Cloud Scale-Out: Expanding In-Memory Capacity Beyond Single-Node Limits
entry.content:
As data-driven enterprises grow, so does the demand for in-memory processing at scale. SAP HANA Cloud already offers vertical scaling, increasing the size of a single node instance to accommodate growing workloads. But what happens when your dataset simply outgrows what any single node can hold?

SAP is introducing SAP HANA Cloud scale-out as part of its Multi-Dimensional Elastic Scaling strategy: a solution that extends memory capacity horizontally across multiple nodes, while keeping the full simplicity of working with a single HANA instance.

Scale-Out in Context: SAP HANA Cloud's Multi-Dimensional Elastic Scaling

Scale-out completes a broader, multi-dimensional approach to elasticity in SAP HANA Cloud, where different mechanisms address different needs for in-memory data growth:

 

Scaling dimension

Mechanism

When to use

Vertical

Scale-up

Growing data that still fits on one node

Temporary burst

Elastic Compute Nodes (ECNs)

Predictable workload peaks (e.g. month-end reporting)

Permanent horizontal

Scale-out (planned)

Data volume that permanently exceeds single node capacity

 

What Is SAP HANA Cloud Scale-Out?

SAP HANA Cloud scale-out is a permanent horizontal scaling capability that distributes a single HANA Cloud instance across multiple nodes, one coordinator node and multiple worker nodes operating together as a shared-nothing cluster.

Data including tables and partitions is distributed across all nodes. The coordinator node orchestrates query execution and manages cluster-wide operations, while all nodes participate equally in storing data and processing queries in parallel. Despite this distributed internal architecture, the system presents itself to applications as a single SAP HANA Cloud instance: same SQL interface, same connection endpoint, no application workflow changes required.

 

 

Key Capabilities

Permanent Scaling – breaking the maximum in-memory size limitation of data holding for HANA Cloud instance, enable very large size for high performance compute.

One instance with multiple nodes– data distributed among coordinator and workers, and operate as one internal shared-nothing cluster, yet appear to user as a single large HANA instance behaving identically to a single-node instance.

Online Flexible Scaling – Add worker nodes to expand memory capacity and query concurrency, or remove workers and resize nodes to right-size the instance. Now you can choose the node size and number of workers that best match the memory and CPU requirements of your workload, giving you more flexibility to find the right SAP HANA Cloud configuration. These changes can be performed online and remain transparent to applications, so capacity can evolve with the business without downtime.

Migration Tool Support – Reduce manual effort for migrating existing SAP HANA Scale-Out systems to SAP HANA Cloud by streamlining the migration process.

-------

entry.title: What’s Next with SAP HANA Cloud – SAP TechEd 2026
entry.content:
SAP TechEd 2026 is here, and once again, SAP HANA Cloud is at the center of the action! Building on the innovations introduced at TechEd 2025 and throughout the year, we're continuing to push the boundaries of what's possible with enterprise data and AI. As the Database for Business AI, SAP HANA Cloud provides a powerful foundation for building intelligent applications, connecting business data, and enabling the next generation of AI-driven innovation.

Across the SAP Business AI platform, three layers of contextualization power your AI use cases. The first is the SAP Knowledge Graph, with fifty years of SAP process knowledge, encoded and ready for Joule. The second is SAP Business Data Cloud, delivering governed data products with rich semantics. And the third, uniquely powerful, is a custom knowledge layer built with SAP HANA Cloud: your domain ontologies, your entity relationships, your business context, fully customer-managed, running natively inside SAP HANA Cloud's multi-model engines. By combining graph, vector, and SQL retrieval, SAP HANA Cloud helps AI agents access the enterprise context they need to deliver more accurate, relevant, and actionable results.

And there's much more to discover! From agentic capabilities accessible through Joule to the newly released SAP Agent Memory Service, which enables AI agents to retain context across sessions and workflows, SAP HANA Cloud continues to expand what's possible with Business AI. The new Time Series Foundation Model also brings on-the-fly predictions directly into the database, without requiring model training. With even more innovations on the horizon before the end of 2026, there's plenty to explore at SAP TechEd this year!

Read on to explore all the major announcements from SAP TechEd 2026.

 

SAP HANA Cloud Admin Agent — Now Integrated with Joule

Managing an SAP HANA Cloud instance demands deep expertise: diagnosing memory growth, tracing out-of-memory situations buried in calculation views, navigating multi-step version upgrades at odd hours. The new SAP HANA Cloud Administration Agent brings expert-level operational intelligence directly into these workflows, in natural language. Describe what you need, whether that's understanding why your database is running slow, identifying optimization opportunities, or scaling systems down after business hours, and the agent investigates, diagnoses, and recommends a course of action for you to approve. It is designed for SAP HANA Cloud administrators, DBAs, and cloud operations teams: you don't need to be an SAP HANA expert to get expert-level outcomes, but if you are, the agent handles the administrative groundwork so you can focus on the decisions that matter! Learn more in this blogpost by @jose_at_sap 

 SAP HANA Cloud Administration Agent in Joule

Agent Memory Service

Every AI agent session starts from scratch, and for enterprise deployments, that is a costly problem! Agents re-ask questions already answered, forget user preferences established in previous interactions, and lose track of in-progress workflows after a timeout. With the General Availability of SAP Agent Memory Service in Q3 2026, this fundamental limitation is addressed head-on. Built on SAP HANA Cloud's vector engine, the service provides a fully managed, persistent memory layer for AI agents on SAP Business AI Platform: agents can store knowledge across sessions, retrieve it semantically at the right moment, and maintain a governed, auditable log of their interactions, all within the same trusted SAP HANA Cloud instance that already powers your business data. The result is agents that remember user preferences, pick up workflows where they left off, and grow sharper over time without retraining, while keeping prompts lean and enterprise governance intact. Read this blogpost by @shabana   to explore how it works and how to get started.

Access by Through Joule Studio Runtime (App Fnd) for native in-house SAP developer experience

 

 

Subscription as a stand-alone SAP BTP Service tied to your SAP HANA Cloud instance

 

 

Time Series Foundation Model (RPT-TS)

At SAP TechEd 2026, we're excited to unveil SAP-RPT-TS! A breakthrough time series forecasting foundation model and the newest member of the SAP-RPT AI model family, built to bring enterprise-grade forecasting directly to SAP HANA Cloud. Where traditional large language models fall short on the structured data that drives your business, SAP-RPT-TS is purpose-built for it. It can deliver accurate, zero-shot forecasts for demand, sales, revenue, and inventory with no model training, no tuning, and no data science overhead. Simply supply a snapshot of your historical data, and the model generates production-quality forecasts on the fly, complete with calibrated prediction intervals that quantify uncertainty, so your teams can act with confidence and avoid the cost of over- or under-forecasting. It handles the messy realities of real-world data automatically, from missing values and seasonality to multivariate series, and runs natively within SAP HANA Cloud on cost-effective CPU infrastructure. No expensive GPUs required! Best of all, you can get started in just a few lines of code with hana_ml, or explore it instantly in the RPT Playground. With SAP-RPT-TS, world-class forecasting is now built right into the platform you already trust.

 Try out SAP-RPT-TS via the SAP RPT Playground now

Learn more about our new Time Series Foundation Model in this blogpost by @ChristophMorgen

 

Scale-Out Support for SAP HANA Cloud

SAP HANA Cloud Scale-out is one of the capacity increasing solutions that SAP HANA Cloud will provide for Elasticity & Scalability. It is the permanent horizontal scaling using multiple worker nodes and one coordinator node to work together internally as a shared-nothing cluster system to provide large memory capacity. It is one large-size HANA instance that behaves the same as single node HANA instance.  Beyond addressing the in-memory data size limitations of a single node, scale-out gives customers greater flexibility to find the right SAP HANA Cloud configuration for their specific workload requirements, allowing them to combine multiple nodes to achieve the precise balance of node size and performance class that their workload demands. In a scale-out system, all nodes operate under a main coordinator node, working together to process user queries and tasks. Data, including tables and partitions, is distributed across the nodes, enabling the query optimizer to leverage parallel execution for faster processing of queries involving large tables.

Learn more about Scale-out in this blogpost by @zhen_tian

 

Real-Time Event-Driven Architectures and Agents

with SAP HANA Cloud and SAP Integration Suite, advanced event mesh

What is smarter than an AI agent? An event-driven AI agent. The standard agent pattern is reactive: a user types, an agent responds. But business reality does not wait for prompts. So, let us make agents event-driven through three phases:

Sense: data crosses a threshold, a process reaches a critical state, something shifts in your landscape. SAP Integration Suite, advanced event mesh captures these signals (events) the moment they happen, propagating them in real time across your entire landscape, without polling that burns unnecessary compute and tokens.

Contextualize: those events hit a multi-model custom knowledge layer built with SAP HANA Cloud, spanning vector search, knowledge graphs, relational data, and in-database AI. Agents reason over live business data, understanding not just that something changed, but what it means, to respond accurately.

Respond: the right agents are activated through SAP Integration Suite, advanced event mesh, each acting according to its role in the business process with the right business context, with no manual trigger needed.

Data scientists and integration experts collaborate to build and maintain event-driven agentic architectures, keeping business context current within the custom knowledge layer. This includes defining how events map to agent actions and which agents handle which scenarios, enabling use cases from dynamic pricing and fraud detection to supply chain optimization and predictive maintenance. With improved interoperability between SAP HANA Cloud and SAP Integration Suite, Advanced Event Mesh planned for Q4 2026, this capability is only getting sharper.

Exciting innovations are ahead as SAP HANA Cloud continues to pave the way for the agentic future! Make sure to follow the SAP HANA Cloud tag for updates on the latest developments, and check out #whatsnewinsaphanacloud for new blog posts, technical deep dives, and product news.

To dive deeper into recent innovations and latest webcasts, watch our curated YouTube playlist.

Finally, be sure to join the SAP HANA Cloud Community. It's a great place to ask questions about the topics covered at SAP TechEd 2026, learn more about SAP HANA Cloud, and discuss the innovations highlighted in this blog with our experts and fellow community members.

Thank you for being part of the SAP HANA Cloud journey.

We look forward to seeing how you bring these innovations to life and build what matters!

Salve, comunidade CWB!

Luiz Souza por aqui! Esse ano consegui encaixar na agenda para acompanhar o SAP TechEd 2026 pelo virtual — de Curitiba mesmo, café na mão e duas telas abertas. E valeu cada minuto. O que aconteceu hoje em Berlim?

O SAP TechEd 2026 começou hoje em Berlim e o primeiro dia já veio carregado. O evento vai até quarta-feira (29/10) e pode ser acompanhado de graça na versão virtual. Aqui vai o resumo do Day 1 para quem quer ficar por dentro sem precisar assistir tudo.

 

O Developer Garage 

Logo no começo da transmissão do SAP Developer News, a gente já vê o Developer Garage — aquele espaço hands-on onde o pessoal senta, abre o laptop e sai testando as novidades com zero pressão. Tutoriais prontos, ferramentas carregadas e os Developer Advocates ali do lado ajudando. Confesso que deu uma inveja boa de quem estava lá presencial.

 

Um "guardião" para toda a IA da empresa

Essa parte me chamou atenção assistindo a cobertura: a SAP anunciou o SAP Enterprise AI Gateway — basicamente um painel de controle central para tudo que envolve IA na empresa. Quem acessa o quê, quais modelos estão rodando, quanto está sendo consumido e se está tudo dentro das regras.

Faz sentido: quando a empresa começa a usar vários agentes e modelos de IA ao mesmo tempo, o risco de perder o controle cresce. O gateway resolve isso com uma camada única de segurança, monitoramento e auditoria. Funciona com protocolos abertos (MCP e A2A), então agentes de diferentes fornecedores podem trabalhar juntos sem perder a governança. Planejado para Q1 2027.



A IA da SAP agora faz, não só sugere

A keynote foi o ponto alto da transmissão. A frase que ficou: a SAP está passando de uma IA que aprende o negócio para uma IA que opera o negócio.

O Joule Work é o melhor exemplo disso. Você descreve um objetivo e agentes de IA planejam os passos e executam tudo no landscape SAP, de ponta a ponta. Assistindo de casa, deu pra sentir a energia do auditório quando mostraram isso ao vivo.

Outro momento que parei o café pra prestar atenção: o SAP-RPT-2.0, modelo de IA para dados estruturados, agora detecta anomalias automaticamente e faz previsões de negócio sem precisar de um projeto de ML do zero. E em parceria com a HPE, esse modelo foi levado para a Estação Espacial Internacional — sim, rodando a bordo, prevendo falhas em equipamentos sem enviar dados de volta à Terra. Ficção científica virou realidade.

Bônus: a certificação Joule Studio Developer está gratuita até 31 de dezembro de 2026. Já anotei aqui.

ABAP está mais vivo do que nunca

Como alguém que vem do ABAP clássico, essa parte me pegou. O recado foi claro: o ABAP não vai embora — ele está evoluindo com IA.

O ABAP MCP Server permite que qualquer ferramenta de IA interaja diretamente com sistemas ABAP. O desenvolvimento em VS Code ganha suporte cada vez maior. E o SAP-ABAP-1, modelo de IA treinado no código ABAP da própria SAP, já está disponível para ajudar a escrever código, gerar testes e acelerar migrações.

Para quem, como eu, está na jornada do clássico para o moderno: as ferramentas que vão turbinar nosso dia a dia estão chegando — e muitas já estão disponíveis.

Amanhã tem mais — e você também pode assistir

O Day 1 foi só o começo. Amanhã (28/10) continua com sessões técnicas, workshops e mais anúncios — incluindo a noite de celebração dos 30 anos do SAP TechEd.

Eu vou estar acompanhando de novo pelo virtual e trazendo os destaques. Se você ainda não se registrou, a versão online é gratuita e dá acesso às keynotes ao vivo e ao conteúdo on demand depois.
